answer: A survey market mapping yarrow, vine and reef habitats could require each earning key to solve a fresh epoch puzzle before admission. The puzzle commits to that key and an unpredictable public beacon; validators cheaply check its proof and reject reuse. Each added alias must expend separate computation and electricity, even across a parallel farm. Set the expected cost above the extra identity reward; sharing proofs then cannot subsidize clones. This assumes an unbiased beacon, no cheap solution shortcut and a credible reward cap. Newcomers can solve one modest puzzle on ordinary hardware.
